title: Fugaro pending steps
description: The local document recording the steps a machine still owes for the management changes made on it (docs/composite-commands, D1562, D1567, D1570, D1575). It sits beside the project config it belongs to, at projects/<name>.pending.json under the config home, and `fugaro apply` is what reads it and runs what it names; `fugaro update` clears the entries of the stages it ran successfully and leaves the rest, a catalog build among them. It is written by the commands that save a change without running its steps (`--no-apply`) and by the steps that failed after the change was saved. Every object here is closed, unlike the schemas of documents a consumer outside this binary reads: the file is read by the same build that wrote it and is decoded strictly (a member this build does not know is an error, CLAUDE.md), so a closed object is what the reader actually does, and a version is what a document from another build is refused on. The one thing the document may never hold is a value: an entry names the change that asked for the step and never what was set (D1570), so the file can never become a second copy of the config or a place a secret is written down.

version.description: The document's own version. A file whose version is not this one is refused rather than read as this version's, and is never written over: a newer fugaro's record of what is owed survives an older one.

last_apply.description: The stamp `doctor` compares: the hash of the project config's bytes at the last apply that finished, absent when none has. It is what tells a machine that owes nothing from one whose file was deleted or lost — a stamp that no longer matches the config, with no pending document, says the config changed since and that nothing owed is recorded (D1575). Neither written nor compared by internal/apply: the caller that has the config in hand does both.

steps.description: What is owed, written even when it is empty: `[]` is "this machine owes nothing", which is a different answer from a document still carrying an earlier change's steps. Two changes that owe the same step leave one entry, so the steps dedupe (spec rule 3).

step.description: The step's name: one of internal/initflow's stage names, or `catalog-build`, the one step that is not a stage — the billable Cloud Build of a catalog image, which `fugaro update` never runs (D1577). The order the steps run in is not this array's: it is internal/initflow's own (Names, Needs), computed when the document is read. It is deliberately not an enum: the vocabulary is initflow's, and a copy of it here would be the second registry of stages D1561 rules out — a stage renamed there would leave this list refusing a step the binary can run.
step.$comment: apply.CatalogBuild in internal/apply/steps.go, and initflow.Names in internal/initflow/stage.go.

project.description: The Fugaro project name the entry was queued for (config.ProjectNameRE). It is half of what makes a file that travelled refuse rather than run: `fugaro apply` compares it with the project it is acting on (D1575).

gcp_project.description: The GCP project ID of the installation the entry was queued in, the other half of that binding (D1575). A document restored into another project's config directory holds entries bound to the installation the changes were made in, and the read refuses them by name.

change.description: The change that asked for the step, shown to the person running `fugaro apply` so the step is not a mystery. It is the change's subject only, never its value (D1570).

kind.description: What `key` names: a key of the settings registry (internal/settings), or a resource type a management command manages.

key.description: The setting key as `fugaro settings` spells it (`image_catalog.entries.*.name`, `layer.defaults.agent.auth`), or a resource type (`image`, `repo`, `workspace`). The table in internal/apply/steps.go is what turns it into the steps the entry names.
